text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rebounded 3.3% today, recovering most of the losses from the prior three trading days. The bounce coincides with oil prices steadying after earlier this week's spike — crude had hit $116 a barrel on geopolitical fears around Iran tensions and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, but today fell back as Saudi Arabia's defense minister traveled to Iran to pursue de-escalation talks. Refiners like Marathon benefit when crude prices are elevated but stable; the whipsaw down and back up this week likely unsettled the stock more than any single price level.

The refining environment remains supportive underneath: U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity utilization, and crude inventories sit at 695 million barrels — levels that allow processors to operate profitably on the current spread between crude input costs and finished fuel prices. The Middle East risk premium that drove this week's volatility hasn't disappeared, so the stock's recovery today reflects relief at de-escalation signals rather than a fundamental shift in the supply picture.
